50983538.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to MD2 (unknown origin) by SPR assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface plasmon: The binding affinity of 1e, 1f, and 2e were determined using the ProteOn XPR36 Protein Interaction Array system (Bio-Rad Laboratories, Hercules, CA) with a HTE sensor chip (ProteOn™, #176-5033). Briefly, MD2 protein (in acetate acid buffer, pH5.5) was loaded to the sensors which were activated with 10 mM NISO4. The compounds 1e, 1f and 2e (at 200, 100, 50, 25, 12.5 and 6.25 μM) were prepared with running buffer (PBS, 0.01%Tween20, 5% DMSO). The samples were then captured in flow cell 1, leaving the second flow cell as a blank. Six concentrations were injected at a flow rate of 30 μl/min for 120s of association phase, followed with 120s of dissociation phase at 25 °C. The final graphs were obtained by subtracting the blank sensor and buffer. Data were analyzed with ProteOn manager software. KD was calculated by global fitting of the kinetic data from various concentrations of 1e, 1f and 2e using 1:1 Langmuir binding model.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Fig. 4. Binding affinity of three active compounds to MD2 protein. (A, B, C) Fluorescence measurements showed that 1e, 1f, and 2e dose-dependently inhibited the binding of bis-ANS and rhMD2. The IC50 value of 1e, 1f and 2e is 4.22 μM, 9.08 μM and 6.83 μM, respectively. (D, E, F) Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis showed that 1e, 1f, and 2e directly bind to rhMD2 in a dose-dependent manner. RhMD-2 was loaded onto the HTE chip and various concentration of compounds flow through the surface of the chip. The response unit were collected and calculated by global fitting of the kinetic data using Langmuir binding model. The KD value of 1e, 1f and 2e is 189 μM, 125 μM and 84 μM, respectively.
original_paragraph.Results Section - 2.5 Kinetic analysis o: We performed the SPR assay to quantitatively determine the kinetic constants of the active derivatives binding to MD2 protein in BioRad ProteON XPR36. SPR is a useful technique to monitor molecular interaction in real time and the technique has been applied to investigate the interactions between small molecular ligands and protein [27]. Briefly, MD2 protein was immobilized onto a HTE chip and various concentrations of active compounds were used as analytes. Fig. 4D–F shows the SPR sensor response unit of 1e, 1f, and 2e binding to the MD2. The KD value was calculated by global fitting of the kinetic data from various concentrations of compounds using Langmuir binding model. Three compounds showed dose-dependent binding to the MD2. The KD value of 2e (84 μM) was 2.25-fold lower than that of 1e (189 μM), while 1f showed a moderate KD value (125 μM).
